One actor per native run,12 instants. Two constitutional controls differ only in
clearance:100 versus400 per elapsed step. Both start with burden0; identical
external intoxicant800 arrives at consequence7. Current choice and execution7
precede that exposure. At8 prior exposure has cleared to700 or400, respectively.
The sober control receives no exposure. Sleep accumulation/night drive/fuel and
water drain0, stress baseline0/arousal500, no injury or exogenous stress. Regulatory
adaptation gains0. These are finite candidate units, not substance concentrations
or elapsed hours. No pharmacological, dose-response or clinical calibration claim.

rows.text:
Common competence300 and control threshold800 are independently declared. Native
execution requires challenge strictly less than competence; control inhibition uses
capacity greater than or equal to threshold. Preserve this contract-specific boundary
instead of borrowing the different SKILL profile's inclusive execution convention.
At slow-clearance probes8..12, challenge350/300/250/200/150 and control650/700/750/
800/850 discriminate execution recovery10 from inhibition recovery11. The final
slow body still has burden300; functional recovery is not complete bodily clearance.

rows.text:
The shared prelude practices the reward action at1 and admits one outcome receipt.
Catalog key drug has reward600 but zero intoxicant/injury; intoxication is a separate
external source. At2 a common load800 permits a genuine two-option protective contest,
importance600. Only that expression can qualify acquired identity. From3 onward
load0, no further outcome receipts, identity learning disabled. Original nonzero
identity journal and learned outcomes must remain byte-identical within seed across
constitutions/exposures. Probe options are drug/withhold at8..12; between acquisition
and probes only withhold is offered. Goals remain adopted and maintained throughout.

competence850 changes only execution for the same slow-clearance history at seed1;
first exposed appraisal and intent must match, although later reward sensation may
legitimately diverge after successful versus failed reward execution. Interference
blocks sober probe execution without changing control; inert withholding preserves
whole observer output for that specific control.

BlindSober/BlindSlow deny intoxication and downstream reward/pleasure/withdrawalReward
from3 onward. Denying intoxication alone is insufficient to demand whole-view equality:
failed reward execution may change later admitted reward signals. Under the declared
four-channel mask, hidden burden/execution may differ while the entire safe stream
must remain byte-equal. This tests conditional noninterference, not invisibility of
all consequences of intoxication. FalseSober supplies biased zero intoxication despite
the slow physical source; inhibition may remain effective while execution fails.

First compare a rested, sleep-deprived and recovered trajectory, with identical
constitution and previously acquired identity/competence/goal state at the matched
probe. Preserve the losing or temporarily unmaintained goal rather than retire it.
Manipulate sleep pressure independently from intoxicant, stress, task load and
interference. Compare native Full versus NoControl where appropriate; distinguish
inhibition/access change from execution impairment and current motivation. A matched
sensor-blind or biased condition must not grant hidden body truth to cognition.
